agree.reason: A household that left because the farm went quiet and gave no credit gets a plain apology and two concrete fixes for exactly those failures, so it would seriously consider signing up again.

honest.reason: Every claim matches the brief and the facts the user supplied, including the limits of the nets and the refusal to promise no loss, and no number is invented.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only repeated, never worked out: the email doesn't show that the new rule would have credited roughly $74 for last summer's six half-boxes (about $24.50 a week), and it leaves out the survey result that 29 of 41 said they'd return on this fix.

right_comparison.reason: The email sets this year against last year's handling but never compares what the reader gives up or risks by not signing up, and it doesn't show what last summer would have looked like under the new credit rule.

qualification.reason: The hedges are concrete and checkable: credit kicks in when a box is cut by more than a third, emails go out every Thursday, the nets don't cover the greens, and sign-up closes March 15 with 52 shares left, though it doesn't say how a one-third cut is measured.

objections.reason: Both halves of the reader's complaint, the silence and the lack of credit, are answered head-on, and the email doesn't stop to argue objections the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a properly formed email of about 195 words, just under the 200-word limit, but a stray '</invoke>' tag is left at the end.
